decisions.reason: TS runs arbitrary JavaScript in a VM sandbox; Go has no equivalent and the port deliberately omits it
TS hot-reloads a single command module from disk; Go commands are compiled in, so /buttons_reload covers the command menu instead

the old bot sends a user without access an encrypted request key that the user returns to be accepted, and its admin command only flips a chat; the Go port has no request-key flow (which is also why it has no /decryptKey) and grants access with an explicit /acceptBot <id>
Go port adds /alias for lesson alias management (TS kept aliases inside the settings scene)
Go port adds archive statistics for the SQLite timetable archive
Go port adds a test command printing the chat record

the old bot keeps /createApiKey out of the Telegram command menu and its argument parser rejects the command word, so it only ever prints the usage hint; the Go port registers the command and implements the whole key lifecycle for its own REST API (issue, rotate, per-key rate limit, last usage, /api and /api_new in the private chat)

Go port keeps /trigger for the day notification run (NextDayUpdater) and adds a manual parser run through /forceparse; the day run is wired only while telegram.noticer is on, so with notifications disabled the command answers 'not found' instead of running the updater like TS always could
Go alias menu uses its own callback root; TS kept alias removal outside the callback list
